title: When anger takes over
issueStatement: Heat rises fast, and the mind starts calling reaction honesty, urgency, or strength.
centralInsight: Gurbani names anger as fire that burns discernment. The answer is not suppression but cooling through Naam, humility, and disciplined speech.
practicalReflection: Anger often borrows the language of justice while quietly centering the injured self. Real strength appears in the pause where heat no longer owns the tongue.
actionPrompt: Before the next hard reply leaves your mouth, slow the body, repeat one line of Naam, and give the moment one more breath.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: When anger keeps choosing the tone of the day
daily.issueStatement: Nothing explosive may happen, yet irritation keeps getting the first word: at home, in traffic, in messages, in the body. The ordinary day becomes easier to scorch than to bless.
daily.centralInsight: Gurbani treats anger as fire because it changes the atmosphere long before it becomes an event. Daily anger is healed by earlier cooling, not by later regret alone.
daily.practicalReflection: The soul often notices anger only when speech hardens. By then the body has already been teaching the room what spirit is leading it.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: When anger wants to spend pressure on someone nearby
pressure.issueStatement: The body is hot, the mind is fast, and pressure is looking for a target. Under strain, anger tries to convert inner pressure into outer force so the self can feel briefly relieved.
pressure.centralInsight: Gurbani cools anger by refusing its claim to authority. Heat is not clarity. The pressure in the room may be real, but the right to wound with it is not.
pressure.practicalReflection: Anger under pressure often feels morally efficient. Yet the soul usually reaches for force first when it is most frightened of being small, exposed, or crossed.
pressure.actionPrompt: When the heat rises, delay the discharge: do not send, say, or decide the first thing anger wants to make permanent.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: When anger rises quickly after the slip
repair.issueStatement: Heat rises fast, and the mind starts calling reaction honesty, urgency, or strength. The break has already happened, and now the temptation is to hide, explain, harden, or turn the miss into identity.
repair.centralInsight: Gurbani names anger as fire that burns discernment. The answer is not suppression but cooling through Naam, humility, and disciplined speech. After the miss, Gurbani keeps the way back near humility, truthfulness, and the next faithful act.
repair.practicalReflection: Repair after anger requires more than cooling down. It asks whether the wound anger made will now be faced with humility, confession, and a refusal to let force remain the last word.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: When anger needs a repeatable shape
practice.issueStatement: Heat rises fast, and the mind starts calling reaction honesty, urgency, or strength. Inspiration is not the main need now; a repeatable return is.
practice.centralInsight: Gurbani names anger as fire that burns discernment. The answer is not suppression but cooling through Naam, humility, and disciplined speech. What is repeated with honesty begins to retrain the reflex itself.
practice.practicalReflection: Anger weakens when the body learns an earlier interruption than the mouth. A practiced pause, kept before the heat becomes speech, gradually retrains what anger expects to own.
